correctness.rationale: Exact unrestricted-parameter Lie computation gives d(z+xy)/dt=(a+1)x^2-y^2, independently recomputed. For a<=-1 bounded forward P is monotone decreasing, and omega-limit invariance with P constant forces x=0 (also at a=-1), then y=z=0, hence convergence. A bounded complete orbit obeying one-sided Q cannot be nonstationary because P is bounded monotone, alpha/omega limits lie in maximal invariant part of Q=0. On cone Q=0 for a>-1, write y=eps sqrt(a+1) x; flow tangency requires z=eps x/sqrt(a+1), but z' along that branch simultaneously equals x/(a+1) and -2x^2, excluding any nonconstant cone-contained entire orbit. Both time limits of P then are 0, forcing origin if Q has fixed sign throughout. Invariant measure condition follows by h(P) test functions and disintegration. No finite-time ODE integration is invoked.
residual_risks: Requires boundedness for long-time claims; does not exclude unbounded trajectories or assert recurrence for every a>-1.
The conditional identity is almost sure for compactly supported invariant probabilities.

value.rationale: A sharp, nontrivial recurrence-exclusion boundary for a canonical time-reversible jerk example, together with a necessary cone-crossing mechanism above it, meaningfully classifies bounded dynamics beyond local equilibrium linearization or computer attractor plots.
residual_risks: Results are conditional on boundedness and do not prove chaotic attractor existence.

final_claim: For reversible jerk dx=z,dy=x,dz=a x^2-y^2-yz, P=z+xy satisfies P'=(a+1)x^2-y^2. When a<=-1 all bounded forward solutions converge to origin and no nontrivial bounded complete orbit exists; for a>-1 every nonstationary bounded complete orbit crosses both strict sides of cone (a+1)x^2=y^2, and compact stationary measures have E[y^2|P]=(a+1)E[x^2|P].
limitations: No existence of periodic/chaotic dynamics in a>-1 sector, only necessary crossing for any nonstationary bounded complete orbit.
